title: multi-probe-failure-classifier-and-automated-mitigation-manifest
author: Aisha Khan
body:
Summary

This document specifies the Multi-Probe Failure Classifier (MPFC) and the accompanying automated mitigation manifest. MPFC is a lightweight, explainable classifier that aggregates heterogeneous probe signals (functional, coherence, latency, token-economy, and quant-sensitivity probes) to categorize degradations and drive deterministic mitigation actions. The goal is to reduce time-to-recovery for production quality incidents while limiting blast radius for safety and customer-facing regressions.

Scope

- Applies to all model-serving promotion targets (hosted, dedicated, and private) where probe telemetry is ingested into the central eval mesh.
- Focused on runtime performance and output quality regressions that can be observed via probe families (see Definitions).
- Not intended for manual labeling pipelines, data privacy incidents, or infra-only failures (see Exception list).

Definitions

1. Probe: an automated query or synthetic interaction designed to exercise a specific slice of behavior (e.g., few-shot instruction consistency, long-context coherence, embedding similarity).
2. Signal: a numerical or categorical feature emitted by a probe (e.g., pass/fail, perplexity delta, embedding cosine, token delta).
3. Failure class: high-level category assigned by MPFC (coherence-drift, hallucination-spike, latency-tail, quant-artifact, behavioral-flip, routing-fallback).
4. Mitigation: an automated operational action (e.g., rollback, throttle, route-to-variant, degrade-quant, increase-batch-window, open-chan).

Failure taxonomy and classifier design

- Coherence-drift: Multi-turn context coherence drops, measured via turn-level coherence score delta > 8% and increase in repetition metric.
- Hallucination-spike: Increased factually-incorrect outputs flagged by synthetic fact-check probes (false positive rate increase > 5% absolute).
- Latency-tail: P95 latency > 800ms or P99 > 2s for gen endpoints serving SLO-sensitive routes.
- Quant-artifact: Sudden rise in token-level inconsistency between float and quant shadow runs (disagreement ratio > 3%).
- Behavioral-flip: Deterministic change in a labeled prompt family where label accuracy drops > 7%.
- Routing-fallback: Increased fallback-to-secondary-model events > 4% of traffic.

Classifier inputs and feature engineering

- Inputs (examples): ["p95_ms", "p99_ms", "coherence_delta_pct", "repetition_score_delta", "fp_rate_delta", "token_disagreement_pct", "fallback_rate", "embedding_shift_cosine", "kvcache_hit_rate"].
- Time windows: compute short (5m), medium (1h), and trend (24h) aggregates. Classifier uses delta between short and trend windows to detect sudden shifts.
- Explainability: MPFC outputs a top-3 contributing signals per classification for operator triage.

Alerting and thresholds

- Severity levels: P1 (customer-impacting, auto-mitigation allowed), P2 (degrades SLOs, require review before mitigation), P3 (informational).
- Example thresholds (configurable per-service):

| Metric | P1 threshold | P2 threshold | Note |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| p95 latency (ms) | >1200 | 800-1200 | SLO-sensitive routes only |
| coherence_delta_pct | >10% | 5-10% | measured on prioritized slices |
| fp_rate_delta | >6% abs | 2-6% abs | applies to fact-check probes |
| token_disagreement_pct | >5% | 2-5% | comparing quant vs float |

Automated mitigation flow (high level)

1. Detection: Probe mesh emits a trigger event when classifier score >= configured severity threshold.
2. Enrichment: MPFC fetches recent traces, model version tags, rollout state, shadow cohort metrics, and last-deploy commit.
3. Scoring: Compute confidence and top-3 reasons; determine allowable mitigations based on service policy.
4. Action: Execute mitigation (examples below). Actions are conditionally gated by safety checks and cooldown windows.
5. Post-action evaluation: Run focused sanity probes (micro-slice) against mitigated traffic and hold for 10 minutes. If metrics improve, create an incident record and schedule manual review; if not, revert mitigation.

Mitigation action catalog (examples)

- Route-to-variant: Move 30%→0% traffic to the variant causing issues and redistribute to stable baseline.
- Auto-rollback: Switch active model version to previous stable version if regression type in [behavioral-flip, hallucination-spike] and confidence > 0.9.
- Degrade-quant: For quant-artifact class, switch to higher-precision quant or fallback to float path for 10% of requests.
- Throttle/buffer: For latency-tail, enable increased batching up to 2x and return 503 on overflow edges to protect SLOs.
- Canary-throttle: Reduce canary weight from x% to x/2% and trigger shadow replay for failing probes.

Runbook: step-by-step automated mitigation procedure

1. Receive MPFC P1 event -> run enrichment and compute mitigation candidates.
2. Verify no active security flags in last 24h (if flags present, escalate to SRE + Security and do not auto-mitigate).
3. If confidence >= 0.9 and policy allows auto-rollback, trigger rollback via deployment api:

   curl -X POST https://infra-api.internal/v1/deployments/rollback 
   -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN' 
   -d '{"service":"text-gen","target_version":"v1.14.2","reason":"mpfc-auto-rollback"}'

4. If mitigation is route-to-variant, call traffic-router patch with safety envelope: reduce by 30% max per minute and monitor micro-probes.
5. Post-action: run 3 focused probes from the failing slice and wait 10 minutes. If all three pass thresholds, create a templated incident and page the owner_team with summary and top-3 reasons.
6. If the mitigation fails to improve metrics after 2 attempts, escalate to on-call product+ml owner.

Configuration reference (example service-level manifest)

| field | type | allowed values | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| service | string | service name | none | logical service id to apply MPFC |
| severity_policy | object | P1/P2/P3 buckets | company-default | mapping of classifier score -> actions |
| auto_mitigate | boolean | true/false | false | global opt-in toggle per service |
| cooldown_minutes | integer | 0-1440 | 30 | cooldown between mitigations |
| allowed_actions | list | [rollback,route,degrade-quant,throttle] | [route,throttle] | permitted automated actions |

Safety and constraints

- Auto-mitigation is disabled for services with high-risk labels (safety, compliance, billing).
- Any rollback that changes persisted state or customer-visible outputs requires a must-pass sanity probe set.
- Rate-limited: max 2 auto-mitigations per 24h per service to avoid flapping.
- All automated actions produce an audit event with owner, reason, and pre/post snapshots.

Testing and validation

- Unit tests: deterministic classifier tests covering synthetic failure injections.
- Integration: run MPFC in dry-run mode for 14 days against shadow traffic; compare suggested mitigations with human decisions.
- Game-day: quarterly simulation where we inject a quant-artifact and validate full mitigation loop (detection->action->post-eval->audit).

Observability and dashboards

- Dashboard panels: active mitigations (last 24h), classifier confidence histogram, top failure classes by service, mitigation success ratio.
- Logs: structured mitigation_event records with fields {service, action, confidence, reasons, pre_metrics, post_metrics}.

Ownership and SLOs

- MPFC owner: Applied ML Platform (owner on-call = applied-ml-platform-oncall).
- SLOs: detection latency < 2m (time from probe emission to classifier decision) 99% of the time; auto-mitigation success rate > 75% for P1 events where auto-mitigation is allowed.

Rollout checklist

1. Dry-run for 14 days with mitigation suggestions logged (no actions).
2. Enable auto-mitigations for internal-only services with rollback allowed (canary cohort = 5%).
3. Expand to external services with progressively larger cohorts after manual review cycles.
4. Publish runbook and add training for on-call teams.

Governance and review cadence

- Monthly review of mitigation audit logs and false-positive/false-negative cases.
- Quarterly policy review to adjust thresholds and allowed actions.

{
  "service": "text-gen-prod",
  "timestamp": "2026-02-10T12:03:22Z",
  "class": "coherence-drift",
  "confidence": "0.93",

}

Appendix B — exceptions list

- Any service with label: "privacy-sensitive" or "regulatory-bound".
- Incident with correlated security signals (escalate to Security).
